title: "Research"

::: {.content-section}

My research focuses on the psychoacoustics of the singing voice, acoustic and physiological measures of vocal function, and neurodivergent-inclusive assessment design.

Most of my recent research output comes through mentorship — I supervise MFA and MM students through original studies from question formation to conference presentation. Our lab uses Praat acoustic analysis, Polar H10 heart rate monitoring, RespTrack respiration monitoring, and Python-based data pipelines.

## MFA Research Archive

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**[research.kaylagautereaux.com →](https://research.kaylagautereaux.com){target="_blank"}**

A public-facing, interactive archive of thesis research from the Vocal Arts Pedagogy Lab at Boston Conservatory at Berklee. Browse studies with interactive Plotly visualizations — hover, zoom, toggle, and explore the data yourself. All data confidentialized per Berklee IRB.
:::

## Current and recent research themes

- Acoustic voice quality measures (AVQI, DSI, CPPS, HNR, f0)
- Performance anxiety and cardiac synchrony in vocal auditions
- Gender perception in musical theater singing
- Respiratory coordination during pregnancy
- Animal mimicry and singing voice quality
- Cultural responsivity in voice studio pedagogy
- Neurodivergent-inclusive assessment rubric design
